newsitem.title: UK: GKN drops amid renewed litigation threat.
newsitem.headline: GKN drops amid renewed litigation threat.

text.p: Shares in automotive engineering group GKN Plc dropped on Thursday amid renewed concerns about litigation from franchisees of its Meineke Discount Muffler Shops unit in the U.S., dealers and analysts said.

Market sources said a representative of Meineke franchisees, speaking at GKN's annual shareholders' meeting, had highlighted continued litigation by some franchisees against GKN, after a $601 million award against the UK firm relating to misused advertising fees.

They said some franchisees had signed waivers as part of their contracts with the company but had told the meeting they were continuing to seek damages from GKN, whose shares were down 28-1/2p at 935-1/2 by 1421 GMT -- back towards the 13-month low of 905p set on April 24.
Dealers said it was the Meineke franchisee comments that had upset the stock, after a modestly positive AGM statement from the company.
"The statement read reasonably well, but the whole Meineke issue has come to a head again," said one market-maker.
No-one at GKN was immediately available for comment.

Some analysts said the continuing action had been known about. "It was known about all along, this is no surprise," said one. "The market has just panicked because it thought there was going to be another $600 million award against the company."
